title: Modal Verbs: Requests, Permission and Advice
explanation: Modal verbs are followed by the base verb (no 'to'). Could and would are more polite than can and will: Could you help me? Should gives advice (You should rest). Must and have to say something is necessary (I have to leave at six).
explanationPersian: بعد از فعل‌های مُدال فعل ساده می‌آید (بدون to). Could و would مؤدبانه‌تر از can و will هستند: Could you help me؟ Should توصیه می‌کند (You should rest). Must و have to یعنی ضروری است (I have to leave at six).

examples.english: Could you open the window, please?
I have to get up early tomorrow.

exercises.prompt: Which request is the most polite?
You have a cold. A friend gives you advice: "You ___ stay at home and rest."

commonErrors.feedback: For friendly advice 'should' is better than 'must'.
commonErrors.feedbackPersian: برای توصیهٔ دوستانه should بهتر از must است.

exercises.after: to wear a uniform at work. It is a rule.

exercises.incorrectSentence: She can to swim very well.

acceptedAnswers: Could you open the window, please?
Can you open the window, please?
Would you open the window, please?
Would you mind opening the window?

commonErrors.feedback: After 'Could you' use the base verb without 'to'.
commonErrors.feedbackPersian: بعد از Could you فعل ساده می‌آید، بدون to.

acceptedAnswers: I have to get up early tomorrow.
I must get up early tomorrow.
I've got to get up early tomorrow.
Tomorrow I have to get up early.
I have to wake up early tomorrow.

exercises.prompt: Make it polite, using "Could": "Open the door!"
acceptedAnswers: Could you open the door, please?
Could you please open the door?
